rv.q: ‘Here We Are’ is more broadly funny than the films and also more overtly philosophical, with a recurring theme about the gap between appearances and reality—though it doesn’t go all that deep.
The novelty of attending Sondheim’s final musical and experiencing its non-stop zaniness wear off long before ‘Here We Are’ ends, and the whole thing falls apart.

It’s hard to imagine any staging more perfect than Mantello’s, whose masterful comic blocking includes a final image that’s somehow both haunting and exhilarating. Sondheim didn’t live long enough to see it, but he certainly would have heartily approved if he had.
